tools.name: getSupportThread
tools.description: GET /api/v1/support/threads/{id}. One thread, with its messages. A diagnostic returns a single message authored by `user` carrying the notes and the payload, so a client needs one code path rather than two. `can_reply` says whether this thread will accept a reply right now.

id.description: A composite thread id, e.g. t:9c1e… or d:4b77….

tools.name: listSupportThreads
tools.description: GET /api/v1/support/threads. Support threads, newest activity first. Two kinds of thread. A `ticket` is anything a customer wrote and is a conversation; a `diagnostic` is an automated report and cannot be replied to. Ids are composite and stable: `t:<uuid>` and `d:<uuid>`. `since` matches threads created OR updated at/after the timestamp, so an old thread with a new customer message is returned.

type.description: Only conversations, or only automated reports.

status.description: Only threads currently in this state.

since.description: ISO-8601. Matches creation OR last activity.

page.description: Which page of results, counting from one.

tools.name: patchSupportThread
tools.description: PATCH /api/v1/support/threads/{id}. Change a thread state. Either field, or both. Setting `ai_handling` CLEARS `needs_human` — that is the hand-back gesture, done in one call so there is no window where the assistant owns a thread still flagged for a person. A diagnostic has no conversation, so it accepts only open or resolved and refuses the rest with a 409.

tools.name: replyToSupportThread
tools.description: POST /api/v1/support/threads/{id}/reply. Reply to a customer. Stored with author `ai`. Replying to an `open` thread moves it to `ai_handling`. WHETHER A REPLY IS ALLOWED IS DECIDED IN THE DATABASE, not here: a thread that a person has taken over, that is resolved, or where the customer asked for a person returns 409 with a machine-readable `reason` — one of human_takeover, resolved, needs_human or diagnostic_not_repliable.

id.description: A composite thread id. Diagnostics cannot be replied to.

text.description: The reply. Never write an assistant label into it — the UI renders that from the author field.

tools.name: searchSupportKb
tools.description: GET /api/v1/support/kb. The knowledge base to answer from. Articles generated from the published documentation and the legal documents, so they cannot drift from what a person would be told to read. Query the KB before drafting and answer FROM these; every article carries a url so a reply can link the page rather than paraphrasing it.

q.description: Keywords. Omit to list every article.
